title: Generative Synthesis of Highly Stable Perovskite Nanocrystals via Mesoporous Silica for Full-Spectrum White LED

metadata.authors: Wu, Jiaze; Cai, Haoze; Shen, Pauline; Xu, Joanna; Chen, Yixuan; Banik, Jyotiparna; Matsuura, Naomi; Huang, Kai

source_summary: A template-assisted synthesis of CsPbCl3 perovskite nanocrystals within mesoporous silica nanoreactors enables scalable, stable, and tunable materials—supporting yttrium doping, halide tuning, and lead-free variants—for advanced, full-spectrum optoelectronic applications.
abstract: Perovskite nanocrystals with CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, or I) structure have attracted great attention for developing optoelectronic applications in the past few years. However, their low stability and the limited scalability of current synthesis methods pose major challenges for future applications. Here, a template-assisted strategy is reported for synthesizing CsPbCl3 nanocrystals within mesoporous silica nanoreactors. Powder state CsPbCl3 complex fabricated via this method demonstrated an exceptional solvent stability and allows for yttrium doping to further enhance optical performance. Halide tuning (Cl⁻ to Br⁻) and synthesis of lead-free perovskites such as Cs4Bi2MnCl12 enable broad spectral emission, supporting full-spectrum white LED fabrication. This low-cost, scalable, and reproducible method offers strong potential for advancing perovskite-based optoelectronic technologies. © 2025 The Author(s). Small published by Wiley-VCH GmbH.
